forces.title: Shifting news consumption habits towards social media
forces.description: Gen Z primarily uses social media for news, contrasting sharply with Boomers who prefer TV and radio. This generational divergence indicates a structural shift in news consumption away from traditional broadcast channels among younger audiences. While older demographics maintain TV viewership for news, this trend suggests a long-term decline in younger viewers for traditional TV news, necessitating adaptation by broadcasters to digital platforms and diverse content formats to remain relevant across all age groups.

forces.title: Increased Smart TV penetration favoring streaming applications
forces.description: The growth in Smart TV ownership is displacing older, non-smart TV sets. These Smart TVs inherently facilitate easier access to video streaming services (IN040503) and smart set-top boxes, often making app-based content discovery more prominent. This shift means that traditional TV broadcasting (IN040502) faces a headwind as consumers are increasingly routed towards streaming platforms for their video entertainment, potentially reducing direct viewership of linear broadcast channels and impacting the business models of cable and DTH operators.

forces.title: Content discovery shifting from EPGs to in-app search
forces.description: A significant structural shift is observed in how TV audiences discover content. Instead of using Electronic Programming Guides (EPGs) on traditional TV, consumers are now most commonly starting their search within specific applications. This 'usurping' of the EPG by apps (primarily streaming apps, IN040503) presents a fundamental challenge for IN040502 operators, who traditionally rely on EPGs for content visibility, demanding new strategies for content discoverability and audience engagement within an app-centric ecosystem to maintain viewership.

forces.title: Audience acceptance of AI for non-creative TV production tasks
forces.description: UK audiences show a clear acceptance for the use of Artificial Intelligence in repetitive, non-core creative tasks within Film and TV production, while still preferring human involvement in front-end creative roles (on-screen, audio, scriptwriting). This indicates an upside driver for TV broadcasters and content creators to leverage AI for efficiency gains, cost reduction, and faster production cycles in back-end processes, potentially freeing up resources for higher-value creative endeavors and improving profitability margins.

forces.title: Growth of SVOD subscriptions as a primary entertainment choice
forces.description: Despite a slight increase in SVOD churn to 23%, this is more than offset by new subscriptions, with 19% of consumers taking up a brand-new service in the past 12 months. While SVOD falls under IN040503, its sustained growth acts as a significant headwind for IN040502, as it represents a direct competitor for viewer attention and discretionary spending on video entertainment, drawing audiences away from traditional broadcast and cable offerings and increasing the fragmentation of the overall media landscape.

viewpoints.title: Traditional TV remains preferred news source for older demographics
viewpoints.description: The report indicates that a significant portion of the older demographic, specifically Boomers (aged 60-75+), still identifies traditional TV and radio as their most preferred methods to stay updated on news or current events. This generational preference for established media channels provides a degree of stability for TV broadcasters' news programming. While this audience segment is aging, their continued reliance on TV for news offers a consistent, if not growing, viewership base. Broadcasters can leverage this enduring trust and habit among older viewers to maintain a core audience, even as younger generations gravitate towards newer digital news sources, ensuring a foundational demand for traditional news content.

viewpoints.title: Smart TV growth shifts consumption away from older traditional sets
viewpoints.description: Deloitte's survey reveals a trend where the increasing penetration of Smart TVs is actively displacing older, non-smart television sets in UK households. These newer Smart TVs are typically integrated with or provide easy access to a multitude of video streaming services and smart set-top boxes, emphasizing an ecosystem driven by app-based content consumption. This development poses a cautious negative outlook for traditional TV broadcasting (IN040502) as it signals a consumer shift away from relying solely on linear broadcast signals and towards on-demand, internet-delivered content, inherently influencing viewing habits and challenging the sustained relevance of conventional TV hardware.

viewpoints.title: Content discovery shifting from EPGs to streaming application interfaces
viewpoints.description: The report highlights a significant change in how TV audiences discover content: they are increasingly starting their search within specific applications rather than using the traditional Electronic Programming Guide (EPG). This suggests that streaming applications (IN040503) are becoming the primary interface for content selection, effectively 'usurping' the EPG. This trend poses a challenge for traditional TV broadcasters (IN040502) whose content discovery heavily relies on EPGs, forcing them to adapt their distribution and visibility strategies in an app-centric consumption environment, potentially reducing engagement with linear channel schedules.

demand_drivers.description: Older demographics in the UK continue to rely on traditional TV for news, providing a stable, albeit aging, viewership segment for news broadcasters within IN040502.

Growth in Smart TV ownership drives consumers towards integrated digital entertainment, potentially increasing exposure to app-based content discovery over linear TV channels, impacting how traditional TV content is accessed.

new_opportunities.description: Audiences are accepting of AI use in repetitive production tasks for TV content, suggesting opportunities for efficiency gains and cost reduction in content creation and post-production within IN040502.
new_opportunities.opportunity: AI for non-core creative tasks in TV

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of consumer preferences for news sources, device ownership trends, and attitudes towards AI in content creation for Film or TV. While no explicit financial sizing is provided, the analysis details evolving consumption patterns and potential production efficiencies for TV content in the UK.
